items.headline: Intel falls 28.6% in a day, its worst since 1974, on a weak fourth-quarter forecast
items.why: Guidance of $15.0-16.0B revenue and a 38.0% gross margin (from 44.1%), with PC demand weak through at least mid-2027, shows the AI data-center boom is not lifting the PC-exposed part of the chip sector.

sources.title: Stock Market Today October 30, 2026: Tech Stocks Fall as Intel Has Its Worst Day in Decades

items.headline: Alphabet's free cash flow turns negative (-$9.1B) as quarterly capex doubles to $51.4B; Microsoft stays cash-positive
items.why: Alphabet is funding AI build-out with debt (long-term debt up to $125.1B) and guiding 2027 capex to rise significantly, so the market is now pricing financing risk, not just demand, into AI spending.

sources.title: Microsoft and Alphabet Just Reported Earnings, Putting the AI Boom to the Test

items.headline: Semiconductor index drops 7.2% on Friday, ending October down more than 15%, as doubts over AI spending returns spread
items.why: Negative free cash flow at several large cloud spenders is turning the AI supply chain from a momentum trade into a returns-on-capital debate, which is what drove the Nasdaq to its worst month since March 2025.

sources.title: Stock Market Today October 30, 2026: Tech Stocks Fall as Intel Has Its Worst Day in Decades

items.headline: A major exchange hack (about 18,270 BTC) pushes bitcoin to a six-week low near $76,275 and triggers roughly $1.58B in liquidations
items.why: The stolen coins have not moved; if they reach exchanges they add supply on top of $643M of single-day ETF outflows, so the overhang is still live.

sources.title: Bitcoin Price Outlook For November 2026: One Price Level Remains Critical

items.headline: Bitcoin trades near $77,750, down about 8% in a month and about 38% below its October 2025 high of $126,198
items.why: The trend is lower highs and lower lows through autumn, so rallies are currently being sold rather than extended.

sources.title: Current price of Bitcoin for November 2, 2026

items.headline: Bitcoin defends $76,000, the short-term holder cost basis; the daily trend indicator has flipped bearish for the first time since May
items.why: A close below $76,000 exposes $73,000-74,000 and then about $71,000, while reclaiming $81,000-82,000 is the minimum needed to change the picture.

sources.title: Bitcoin Price Outlook For November 2026: One Price Level Remains Critical

items.headline: Fed holds at 3.75%-4.00% with two officials dissenting in favor of a 25bp hike
items.why: Dissents toward tightening, plus an upgrade of activity to a 'strong pace' and inflation still 'elevated', mean the next move is being debated as a hike, not a cut.

items.headline: Futures put the odds of a December Fed rate hike near 75% after ISM manufacturing rose to 55.5
items.why: Strong activity data with prices-paid still at 75.2 keeps rate pressure upward, which is a headwind for long-duration assets such as tech stocks and gold.

sources.title: Gold, silver recover from October rout as oil drops, Fed tightening bets persist - Kitco PM Report

items.headline: US-Iran diplomacy advances: Iran says it has a two-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz; no formal deal announced
items.why: Hormuz is the main driver of the oil risk premium, so an actual reopening would ease inflation pressure while a collapse of talks would reverse the week's oil drop.

sources.title: Gas, diesel, oil prices are down, but reprieve could be temporary

items.headline: Brent settles at $104.77 (-7.6%) and WTI at $96.46 (-7.4%), the biggest one-day drops since July, on Iran talk progress
items.why: The October risk premium is being unwound on headlines alone, with no confirmed supply change, so the move is fragile if talks stall.

sources.title: Gold, silver recover from October rout as oil drops, Fed tightening bets persist - Kitco PM Report

items.headline: Goldman Sachs lifts its December Brent forecast to $105 and warns of a $130 average next year if Gulf output stays constrained
items.why: Even after Monday's drop, a major bank sees prices staying near current levels with a large upside tail, so the drop is not being treated as a trend change.

items.headline: Gold rebounds 1.8% to about $3,946 and silver 3.7% to about $50.80 after an October rout
items.why: Gold needs a hold above $3,817 support and a push through $3,978 resistance to confirm a bottom; a break under $3,817 opens $3,719.

items.headline: S&P 500 closes at 7,580.07 (-1.82%), its biggest one-day drop since June 5 and 3.05% below the 7,818.93 record close of Oct 6
items.why: The index has not yet broken a major structural level, but a third straight weekly loss is the longest losing streak since March.

items.headline: Nasdaq closes at 25,437 (-2.86%) near three-month lows; the semiconductor index breaks below its 200-day average (10,785)
items.why: Losing the 200-day average in the sector that led the market turns the key support into resistance until it is reclaimed.

items.headline: VIX spikes to 23.93 intraday, above the Oct 16 high of 22.31, but closes just under 20
items.why: Fear jumped but did not close at stress levels, and 9 of 11 sectors still rose in October, so this is rotation out of tech rather than a broad breakdown.
